anomalies.observed: R4 (1k, the PWM2 series resistor to servo channel 2 signal) has pin 2 on GND, not on a PWM2 bus net. The spec says R4 runs from the PWM2 GPIO net to J8 pin 3. In PWM mode this grounds the channel 2 servo signal through 1k and leaves no PWM2 source.
anomalies.expected: R4 pin 2 should connect to the PWM2 GPIO net (the same net that R11/R12 should drive), so that J8 pin 3 receives the PWM2 signal from the M5Stack bus.

evidence.quote: R3, R4 | 1k each | Series resistors from the PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets to J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3 respectively.

anomalies.impact: In PWM mode the channel 2 (tilt) servo receives no PWM signal, and its signal pin is tied to ground, so the tilt servo cannot be driven.

anomalies.observed: The R9/R10 jumper pair takes its input from the /PWM1 net. The R11/R12 pair, which should take its input from a PWM2 net, has pin 1 on GND instead. No PWM2 GPIO net exists anywhere in the netlist, so the channel 2 bus-pin selection jumpers are not wired to a signal.
anomalies.expected: R11 and R12 pin 1 should be on the PWM2 GPIO net, mirroring R9/R10 on /PWM1, so that either J1/J2 pin 20 or pin 22 can supply PWM2.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2

anomalies.impact: Channel 2 has no working PWM source from the M5Stack bus, so the second servo cannot be controlled in PWM mode whichever Core variant jumpering is used.

parsed.summary: In the netlist the PWM2 signal path is missing: R4 (J8 pin 3 series resistor) and the R11/R12 bus-pin jumpers all have their PWM2-side terminal on GND, while the equivalent PWM1 path is correctly tied to /PWM1. This breaks PWM channel 2 in the specified PWM mode.
